frontier.hypothesis: The residual is a single PRE-RA multiset-shape decision (not reachable by any spelling of the downstream C tried so far) that determines BOTH the scratchpad-literal materialization count and the y-compare branch topology simultaneously -- likely tied to how GCC's front end lays out the two func_80053614 call sites' argument-passing sequence.
frontier.mechanism: Unknown pre-RA front-end shape (s8's inverse_compose.py classify already proved this is upstream of both ra_solver and sched_solver, i.e. not an allocation or scheduling tiebreak). The next diagnostic step is reading the actual RTL emitted for the two func_80053614 call sites in tmp/grind/func_80056CB8/dumps/text1b.cse2 (captured s6) to see whether the constant's rtx is shared or re-expanded per call, and whether that sharing decision is itself controlled by argument list identity/count rather than by naming.
frontier.next_probe: Try varying the CALL SITE STRUCTURE itself, not just the literal's name: e.g. does wrapping both func_80053614 calls through a single local helper-call site (same call, parameterized by hit array) change the constant's materialization count? Also worth trying: reorder the two calls' surrounding statement blocks (move the r2 call's pt0/pt1 setup earlier, before the r1-dependent x/z adjustment) to see if that changes CSE's basic-block boundary for the constant (see [[cse-block-extension-controls-fold-span]] -- a join label does NOT end cse1's basic block in general, but conditional-branch topology around r1 might).

frontier.hypothesis: The loop-counter register-rotation cluster ($s3 vs target's $s6/$s7-family roles) that s7 originally flagged is NOT a separate axis from the PRE-RA residual above -- s8 already corrected this attribution, but the objdiff region (112 lines at s7) has not been re-read against the current s9-confirmed chassis to see whether ANY of it is now register-only (post-RA) rather than multiset (pre-RA).
frontier.mechanism: s8's classify report characterized the WHOLE residual as pre-RA, but that was measured before this session's dx/dz sub-expression kills; re-running inverse_compose.py classify now (after ruling out three downstream regions) may narrow the multiset diff further or confirm no change.
frontier.next_probe: python3 tools/ra_solver/inverse_compose.py classify text1b func_80056CB8 --target-object build/src/text1b.o --ours-object tmp/sandbox/func_80056CB8/text1b.o on the s9-reconfirmed floor-58 chassis; compare the multiset diff detail against s8's classify_s8.txt to see if it's unchanged (expected, since s9 made no net C change) or whether re-running it now with fresher eyes reveals a lever s8 didn't name.

frontier.mechanism: Same systematic-enumeration modality, applied to a different block: the sin_p/cos_p/scale/x/z computation and the two pt0[]/pt1[] assignment groups preceding each func_80053614 call are candidate regions for a declaration-order or inlining spelling that might change the scratchpad-literal materialization pattern indirectly (by changing what's live across the call, which is what ra_solver models but classify says the diff predates).
frontier.next_probe: Write an ENUM-BEGIN/END region around the pt0[]/pt1[] assignment block preceding the r1 call (6 array-element assignments -- note spelling_enum's regex likely won't parse array-subscript assignments as its 'assignment to outer variable' axis, so this probe may need a small tool patch or a hand-written variant set instead of the automated enumerator).
